title: Sampling changes the choice
summary: Sampling chooses among possible next tokens instead of always picking the highest score. Temperature is one setting that changes how spread out those choices are.
introduction: Sampling chooses among possible next tokens instead of always picking the highest score. Temperature is one setting that changes how spread out those choices are. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Sampling chooses among possible next tokens instead of always picking the highest score. Temperature is one setting that changes how spread out those choices are.

blocks.code:
Low temperature: often favours the highest-scoring choices more strongly
Higher temperature: allows more variety
Still required: check facts and task rules
blocks.title: Sampling changes the choice

blocks.text: This describes a common effect of temperature. Exact behaviour depends on the model and service. Lower variety does not make false information true.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose whether a short data extraction or a playful naming task needs more variety.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Temperature is not an accuracy slider.
